meta.title: Site improvement proposals
meta.policy: Nothing in this register is implemented. Each row is a proposal to improve the site's decision-making value, with its trade-offs and one recommended path. A reviewer records a choice per row (accept / modify / reject) in COORDINATION.md or a GitHub issue before any change is made.

rows.proposal: Refresh the committed data snapshot weekly and stamp every page with the exact as-of date of its inputs
rows.improves: Every downstream decision: stale inputs were the top irregularity of the 2026-11-12 audits (snapshot ended 2026-11-01 while the live slate was Week 10)
rows.cost: low (one scheduled workflow already exists; needs a freshness gate)
rows.tradeoffs: Weekly refresh keeps decisions current but can silently change published numbers between reviews; pinning a release tag per snapshot costs storage but makes any figure reproducible forever
rows.recommended_path: Keep the scheduled refresh, add a CI freshness check that fails when the extract lags the current game week, and render the as-of date in every page header

rows.proposal: Capture timestamped pre-kickoff price snapshots (a real price feed, not just the closing line)
rows.improves: Gate G1 (point-in-time integrity) can then be evidenced at all; without it no strategy can ever pass, and closing-line value cannot be measured
rows.cost: medium (collector service or licensed feed; storage is small)
rows.tradeoffs: A free scraped board costs nothing but is fragile and may violate terms; a licensed feed is reliable but paid. Closing-line-only settlement is honest but structurally cannot demonstrate edge capture
rows.recommended_path: Start with a licensed or officially permitted feed for spreads/totals/moneylines only, timestamped server-side; do not collect player props until the singles market is proven

rows.proposal: Ingest the official injury report and team depth charts as point-in-time features labelled by depth string (1st/2nd/3rd/4th) on both offense and defense
rows.improves: Injury/depth decisions: the requirement is to know when a 2nd-4th string backup replaces a starter, and no lab currently has verified league-wide depth order
rows.cost: medium (snapshot storage; mapping players to depth strings)
rows.risk: medium (league charts are labelled unofficial; missing rows must stay blank, never inferred)
rows.tradeoffs: Team-published charts are easy to fetch but unofficial and inconsistent (only Arizona's is labelled official); an nflverse-derived depth is reproducible but third-party. Both must be labelled by provenance
rows.recommended_path: Store daily snapshots of the official report plus each team's chart with a strict provenance label per row; blank any string a chart does not publish; estimate replacement-level effects only after SI-02 lands

rows.proposal: Name one canonical suggestion review queue and make every lab's register feed it read-only
rows.improves: Decision speed: eight overlapping hubs currently publish suggestions under four different ID schemes, and reviewers cannot see the whole queue in one place
rows.cost: low (aggregation only; no lab content changes)
rows.tradeoffs: A single queue is auditable but becomes a new shared file that every session must not hand-edit; keeping labs independent preserves their context but keeps proposals scattered
rows.recommended_path: Adopt the verify-hub consolidated queue as canonical, link it from every hub, and regenerate (never hand-edit) it from the lab registers

rows.proposal: Render a verification badge (verified / blank-unverified) and a source link in every table row on every lab page
rows.improves: Trust in every number: 28 pages outside the published build still lack per-row source columns and are only link-checked
rows.tradeoffs: Badges make status obvious but add visual noise; strictly blank-unverified cells are honest but leave holes a reader may want filled — the policy says the holes stay
rows.recommended_path: Extend the root table() source discipline (already enforced by tests/check_site.py) to the remaining labs in one pass per lab, with the badge derived from a checked field, never typed

rows.proposal: Require a pre-registration template for every strategy submission (hypothesis, stake rule, gates, evaluation window) committed before evaluation
rows.improves: Skill-vs-luck integrity of the leaderboard: hindsight selection is the main way luck masquerades as skill
rows.cost: low (a template file plus a gate that checks it exists)
rows.tradeoffs: Pre-registration slows experimentation but makes gate G10 (no hindsight) checkable instead of asserted; relaxed modes invite silent threshold tuning
rows.recommended_path: Add the template to the strategy schema and fail gate G10 when a strategy has no pre-evaluation commitment record

rows.proposal: Decide the leaderboard reward question explicitly: fund a pool, publish it as recognition-only, or drop rewards — and clear the Alberta legality question first
rows.improves: The competition design: four conflicting reward schedules exist across labs and no prize is funded, so 'rewards for top strategies' is currently an unfunded claim
rows.cost: low to decide; funding cost is whatever the reviewer chooses
rows.risk: medium (regulatory if money moves; reputational if a prize is promised and not funded)
rows.tradeoffs: Cash prizes attract submissions but trigger gaming-regulator questions by jurisdiction; recognition-only is safe but weaker incentive
rows.recommended_path: Publish recognition-only tiers now (no money, no promises), and keep any funded pool behind a written legal review of the operator's jurisdiction

rows.proposal: Make the landing page decision-first: open with the blocking questions and their owners instead of the research summary
rows.improves: Time-to-decision for a reviewer: the most valuable layer (what to decide next) is currently three clicks deep
rows.tradeoffs: A decision-first front page is faster for reviewers but hides the evidence layout new readers expect; two entry paths (by question / by evidence) cost a little duplication
rows.recommended_path: Add a 'Decide first' panel at the top of the overview linking each open decision to its evidence, without moving the existing sections

rows.proposal: Ship a parlay correlation calculator: enter legs, get the copula-priced joint probability with an interval, compared against naive multiplication
rows.improves: Parlay and prop-combo decisions: the measured QB-WR1 correlations are the site's strongest finding but readers cannot apply them to their own ticket
rows.cost: medium (small static calculator over the measured correlation matrix)
rows.risk: medium (users may read a pricing tool as betting advice; needs the standing disclaimer)
rows.tradeoffs: A calculator is the most used feature but also the easiest to over-trust; showing intervals and the naive price side-by-side mitigates but does not remove that risk
rows.recommended_path: Build it with intervals on every output, the naive product shown next to the copula price, and no stake or bankroll advice anywhere

rows.proposal: Publish a weekly market-benchmark report (closing-line accuracy drift, cover/over rates with intervals) as the early-warning layer for regime change
rows.improves: Detection of market regime changes before any strategy is trusted: a stable-looking edge can be a drifting market
rows.tradeoffs: Weekly reports are cheap but add another artefact to keep consistent with the site; monthly would be quieter but slower to notice drift
rows.recommended_path: Generate it from the same derived JSON the site renders, so the report can never disagree with the published numbers
